body:
## Layered testing policy (maintainer-approved, 2026-11-21)

This refines browser-first acceptance: most behavior should be covered by fast unit tests, with focused integration tests and only a small number of essential UI end-to-end journeys. It supersedes blanket per-issue full-UI or full end-to-end requirements below, without removing product behaviors or accepting known product regressions. Browser-first describes the preferred execution surface when UI verification is necessary, not the default layer for every test.

1. **Unit tests are the default.** Cover meaningful behavior through stable public module interfaces: filtering/sorting/pagination, parsing/render models, search/scopes, validation, draft/lifecycle state transitions, async request fencing and focus/selection restoration decisions. Control time, event ordering and external inputs where needed. Avoid private-method assertions, internal collaborator call counts, implementation mirrors and tests of trivial reversible edits. Do not impose test-count percentages or add cases merely to meet a quota.
2. **Use focused integration tests for real contracts.** Verify storage/repository persistence, indexes, bridge request/response contracts, conflict handling and restart/readback against isolated real adapters. Unit tests with mocked storage cannot establish persistence or cross-module compatibility. Keep these tests below the UI when the contract can be exercised directly.
3. **Keep UI end-to-end tests small and purposeful.** Cover only critical cross-layer journeys and behavior that lower layers cannot establish. Prefer the actual application in a browser preview, with real isolated storage adapters when persistence is involved. Use representative save/readback, search/open/return and discard/recovery journeys instead of multiplying full workflows across every variant. Use focused browser interaction or visual checks for layout, actual DOM focus, caret/selection and browser event wiring; unit tests of restoration decisions do not prove real DOM behavior. Do not repeat the entire unit-test matrix through the UI.
4. **Native checks are exceptional and change-driven.** Apply the retained browser-first host/transport/packaging/resource/lifecycle/OS-integration criteria. Ordinary shared UI native compatibility replay remains a release-level check, not a per-issue gate. Android-specific and standalone Syncthing checks remain deferred. Preserve the distinction between browser, integration, native and physical-input evidence.
5. **Choose validation from the diff and risk.** For each change, identify the public behavior under test, selected layers and why any UI/native checks are needed. Run affected fast tests and relevant integration tests; select focused UI checks where warranted. Reserve the full maintained UI suite for broad shared renderer/state/focus/layout changes, uncertain cross-page impact or release validation, with a concrete reason. Documentation-only policy edits need consistency/diff checks, not app builds or browser/native replay. Do not rerun unrelated suites or duplicate passing evidence without a new change, failure or unresolved concern.
6. **Retain truthful completion gates.** Existing behavioral acceptance, source preservation, independent final-head Standards/Spec reviews and normal merge gates remain. Preserve failed evidence. A known failing product behavior still needs a fix; changing test layers does not make it pass. Record replaced or deferred checks and justify their coverage mapping. Reuse valid existing evidence for unchanged behavior; do not rewrite delivered tests wholesale or delete useful regression coverage merely to change suite ratios.

---

## Browser-first acceptance policy (maintainer-approved, 2026-11-21)

This is an explicit change to the acceptance method for existing and future work. It supersedes earlier blanket requirements for per-issue packaged-Mac, OS-injected keyboard, actual native IME or native clipboard evidence for shared UI behavior. Preserve the requested product behavior, source/data protections, failure records and final-head review requirements.

- For the small set of UI checks selected under the layered policy, validate layout, reading/Markdown, forms, search, browser keyboard navigation, focus/selection/return, save/discard and cross-page journeys in the actual shared application running in a browser preview. Exercise real controls and observable outcomes. Parser/unit tests, static mockups and mocked storage alone do not establish application acceptance.
- Persistence/index/search journeys must use isolated real Markdown/record storage and indexes through the existing repository/storage adapter and bridge contract, with persisted readback and reload/continuation checks as applicable. State exactly which native transport or OS integration the browser adapter does not exercise. Use synthetic/private-safe fixtures; this policy grants no model download or private-note processing consent.
- Native checks remain required when a change affects native host implementation, bridge transport/wiring, packaged/custom-scheme resource loading or allowlists, app lifecycle/termination, OS shortcut registration, system clipboard integration, native text-input/IME integration or platform compatibility. Run only the affected checks. Native packaging/build verification remains applicable when shipped assets or resource integration change. UI code receiving keyboard/composition events alone does not mandate an OS-input replay for every issue.
- For ordinary shared UI issues, move the previous native compatibility/actual-IME/OS-input replay requirements to release-level checks, nonblocking for the individual PR. Record them as deferred by this user-approved policy, never passed. Browser coverage does not prove native integration. For example, #92 still needs actual Mac packaged custom-scheme/bootstrap/resource-security checks because it changes that integration; it does not require replaying every UI journey natively.
- Existing issues #65, #82, #84, #85, #86 and #105 may be accepted on sufficient current-head browser/application-storage evidence plus applicable checks and separate Standards/Spec review when production host integration is unchanged. Reassess old missing-native dispositions under this policy. Actual product regressions, failed browser/storage checks, source loss, required host-integration failures and unknown resource custody still block the affected delivery.
- Do not queue or grant optional native replays for routine UI acceptance. If an owned native test is already running, complete safe cleanup and input/clipboard restoration before releasing custody; do not kill unknown processes or clear a lease by age. The coordinator must reconcile existing #65/#82/#105 GUI requests and ask the original workers for browser-first completion reports instead of continuing the optional native queue. Native test-executor construction is deferred; do not create implementation work for it under this policy.
- Android-specific tests and standalone Syncthing tests remain deferred and nonblocking under the existing policy. Final-head review, six-worker accounting, normal merge gates and dependency availability remain required. Release-level native checks must be reported separately; they do not silently become passed or block unrelated UI PRs.

---

## Parent

Part of #89

## What to build

Migrate Action browse/filter/open/create/edit/status/history and note-or-passage-to-Action journeys. Return from real persisted Actions to the original note or Current Focus context using shared components and existing repositories.

User stories covered: #89 stories 27–28.

The confirmed #89 acceptance seam is real application UI -> existing native bridge/repositories -> isolated Markdown/JSON storage and private indexes -> persisted readback/restart. Reuse existing domain services. React/TypeScript and compiled Tailwind implement the approved restrained light/contextual/C design with a project-owned shadcn-inspired component system. Presentation components receive data/callbacks rather than owning persistence or sending AI requests. English project material; Simplified Chinese application-owned visible/accessibility copy.

Cross-cutting #89 stories 1–13, 20–25, 36–41, 43–44 and 46–48 apply to this named journey. Preserve source bytes, identities/quotes, safe Markdown/read-only task markers, bounded index queries, workspace/entity drafts, immutable revisions, serialized writes and active-task Save/Discard/Continue. Fence async responses by workspace/task/request identity. Cancel queued work only when possible; submitted writes settle with truthful results. Hidden/recovered forms never become implicit save participants. No Electron, schema/storage migration, automatic AI requests, checkbox promotion or unrelated feature implementation.

Consume prerequisite behavior only after its issue is closed and changes are available on fetched main. Re-query native blockers and overlapping PRs before starting. Do not merge, close or rewrite prerequisites. Record component/bridge/overlay/DOM ownership in the inventory. Preserve legacy consumers through explicit stable adapters until their own migration; no two renderers own the same DOM. Focus refinement from #81–#86 must survive adoption without heavy default rings, blanket focus suppression or competing traps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Create/edit/filter/reopen a confirmed Action, inspect immutable history and verify persisted revisions after restart. Preserve existing status, due date, waiting, validation and overdue semantics.
- [ ] Keep quoted evidence, path and source identity exact; retain changed/missing-source handling and originating passage/scroll/focus. No Markdown checkbox is promoted or modified.
- [ ] Expose stable typed Action entry/return contracts for legacy callers and Initiative consumers; use one shared Action editor.
- [ ] Verify invalid/failed save, submitted-write leave, discard, duplicate submission, private recovery and stale responses through the active-task lifecycle, including native exits.
- [ ] Demonstrate the complete named journey in the packaged Mac app using real isolated storage. Assert visible outcomes, source hashes/persisted readback, return context and failure/recovery behavior rather than class names or component internals.
- [ ] Update the catalogue using actual consumed production components/tokens. Verify pointer/keyboard focus, selected/invalid states, long Chinese content, desktop/393px/reduced-height windows, reduced motion, contrast and role-appropriate hit targets with same-state before/after evidence.
- [ ] Run applicable shared/domain/storage tests, maintained UI journeys, TypeScript check, production build and Mac packaging/native validation tied to the delivered head. Include Chinese IME/caret/selection, shortcuts/clipboard, modal containment/restoration and native close/restart where relevant; do not substitute DOM-only assertions for native input evidence.
- [ ] Record relevant baseline/migrated I/O and performance observations and investigate reproducible regressions. Distinguish browser, DOM-native, OS-injected and physical-input evidence. Android-specific tests and standalone Syncthing tests remain deferred by user decision, never reported as passed.
